He pays a hundred pieces of money; could he acquire for himself large estates at so small a price, or anything more shall some nook in which he might live without molestation? Besides, Moses expressly relates that he bought that part on which he had pitched his tent opposite the city. Therefore he possessed neither meadows, nor vineyards, nor stable land. But since the inhabitants did not grant him an abode near the city, he made an agreement with them, and purchased peace at a small price. <note n="115"> <div sID="gen4351" type="x-p"/> “For a hundred pieces of money.” The word rendered pieces of money, <foreign xml:lang="he">קשיטה</foreign>, (<hi type="italic">Kisitah</hi>,) means also lambs; and the price given might have been one hundred lambs; the probability, however, is, that the coin itself was called a lamb, as we have a coin called a sovereign. It is supposed that the coin bore the image of a lamb, perhaps because it was the conventional price at which lambs were generally valued. The testimony of St. Stephen (<reference osisRef="Bible:Acts.7.16">Acts 7:16</reference>) is decisive as to the fact that money was in use. — <hi type="italic">Ed</hi><div eID="gen4351" type="x-p"/> </note> This necessity was his excuse; so that no one might say, that he had bought from man what he ought to have expected as the free gift of God: or that, when he ought to have embraced, by hope, the dominion of the promised land, he had been in too great haste to enjoy it.<div eID="gen4349" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Gen.33.17" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen4348" osisID="Gen.33.17" type="section"/>
entries.f30ee5312ae3553e9e70624081a41757b8dcba8f: <div annotateRef="Bible:Gen.33.20" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Gen.33.20" sID="gen4352" type="section"/> <div sID="gen4353" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20. </hi><hi type="italic">And he erected there an altar</hi>. Jacob having obtained a place in which he might provide for his family, set up the solemn service of God; as Moses before testified concerning Abraham and Isaac. For although, in every place, they gave themselves up to the pure worship of God in prayers and other acts of devotion; nevertheless they did not neglect the external confession of piety, whenever the Lord granted them any fixed place in which they might remain. For (as I have elsewhere stated) whenever we read that an altar was built by them, we must consider its design and use: namely, that they might offer victims, and might invoke the name of God with a pure rite; so that, by this method, their religion and faith might be made known. I say this, lest any one should think that they rashly trifled with the worship of God; for it was their care to direct their actions according to the divinely prescribed rule which was handed down to them from Noah and Shem. Wherefore, under the word “altar,” let the reader understand, by <hi type="italic">synecdoche</hi>, the external testimony of piety. Moreover, it may hence be clearly perceived how greatly the love of divine worship prevailed in the holy man; because though broken down by various troubles, he nevertheless was not forgetful of the altar. And not only does he privately worship God in the secret feeling of his mind; but he exercises himself in ceremonies which are useful and commanded by God. For he knew that men want helps, as long as they are in the flesh, and that sacrifices were not instituted without reason. He had also another purpose; namely, that his whole family should worship God with the same sense of piety. For it behaves a pious father of a family diligently to take care that he has no profane house, but rather that God should reign there as in a sanctuary. Besides, since the inhabitants of that region had fallen into many superstitions, and had corrupted the true worship of God, Jacob wished to make a distinction between himself and them. The Shechemites and other neighboring nations had certainly altars of their own. Therefore Jacob, by establishing a different method of worship for his household, thus declares theft he has a God peculiar to himself, and has not degenerated from the holy fathers, from whom the perfect and genuine religion had proceeded. This course could not but subject him to reproach, because the Shechemites and other inhabitants would feel that they were despised: but the holy man deemed anything preferable to mixing himself with idolaters.<div eID="gen4353" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4354" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21.</hi> <note n="116"> <div sID="gen4355" type="x-p"/> This verse number appears in the Calvin Translation Society edition. It actually is part of verse 20.<div eID="gen4355" type="x-p"/> </note> <hi type="italic">And he called it El-eloh-Israel</hi> <note n="117"> <div sID="gen4356" type="x-p"/> <foreign xml:lang="la">Et vocavit illud, Fortis Deus Israel</foreign>; “the strong God of Israel.” The margin of the English translation is more literal, “God, the God of Israel.” — <hi type="italic">Ed</hi>.<div eID="gen4356" type="x-p"/> </note> This name appears little suitable to the altar; for it sounds as if a heap of stones or turf formed a visible statue of God. But the meaning of the holy man was different. For, because the altar was a memorial and pledge of all the visions and promises of God, he honors it with this title, to the end that, as often he beheld the altar, he should call God to rememberance. That inscription of Moses, “The Lord is my help.” Has the same signification; and also that Ezekiel inscribes on the forms of speaking thereis a want of strict propiety of metaphor; yet this is not without reason. For as superstitious men foolishly and wickedly attach God to symbols, andm as it were, draw him down from his heavenly throne to render him subject to their gross inventions; so the faithful, piously and rightly, ascend from carthly signs that he worshipped no other God than him who had been manifested by certain oracles, in order tha he might distinguish Him from all idols. And we must observe it as a rule of modesty, not to speak carelessly concerning the mysteries and the glory of the Lord, but from a sense of faith, so far indeed, as he is made known to us in his word. Moreover Jacob had respect to his to his prosperity; for since the Lord had appeared to him, on the express condition, that he would make with him the covenant of salvaation, Jacob leaves his monument, from which, after his death, his descendants might ascertain, ttat his religion had not flowed from a dark or obscure well, or from a turbid pool, but from a clear and pure fountain; as if he had engraved the oracles and visions, by which he had been taught, upon the altar.<div eID="gen4354" type="x-p"/><div annotateRef="Bible:Gen.33.20" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen4352" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1. </hi>And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.<div eID="gen4361" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4362" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1. </hi>Et egressa est Dinah filia Leah, quam pepererat ipsi Iahacob, ut viderat filias regionis.<div eID="gen4362" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4363" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2. </hi>And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.<div eID="gen4363" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4364" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2. </hi>Et vidit eam Sechem filius Hamor Hivvaei principis terrae, et tulit eam, et concubuit cum ea, et humiliavit eam.<div eID="gen4364" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4365" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3. </hi>And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.<div eID="gen4365" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4366" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3. </hi>Et adhaesit anima ejus ipsi Dinah filiae Iahacob, et dilexit puellam: et loquutus est ad cor puellae.<div eID="gen4366" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4367" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4. </hi>And Shechem spake unto his father Hamor, saying, Get me this damsel to wife.<div eID="gen4367" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4368" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4. </hi>Et dixit Sechem ad Hamor patrem suum, dicendo, Cape mihi puellam hanc in uxorem.<div eID="gen4368" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4369" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5. </hi>And Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter: now his sons were with his cattle in the field: and Jacob held his peace until they were come.<div eID="gen4369" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4370" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5. </hi>Audivit autem Iahacob, quod violasset Dinah filiam suam: et filii ejus erant cum pecudibus ejus in agro, et siluit Iahacob, donec venirent ipsi<div eID="gen4370" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4371" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6. </hi>And Hamor the father of Shechem went out unto Jacob to commune with him.<div eID="gen4371" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4372" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6. </hi>Egressus est autem Hamor pater Sechem ad Iahacob, ut loqueretur cum eo.<div eID="gen4372" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4373" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7. </hi>And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard <hi type="italic">it</hi>: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter; which thing ought not to be done.<div eID="gen4373" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4374" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7. </hi>Porro filii Iahacob venerunt de agro: qui quum audierunt ipsi, dolore affecti sunt viri, iratique sunt valde: quia flagitium designasset in Israel, ut coiret cum filia Iahacob: et sic non fiet.<div eID="gen4374" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4375" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8. </hi>And Hamor communed with them, saying, The soul of my son Shechem longeth for your daughter: I pray you give her him to wife.<div eID="gen4375" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4376" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8. </hi>Et loquutus est Hamor cum eis, dicendo, Sechem filii mei complacuit anima in filia vestra: date quaeso eam illi in uxorem.<div eID="gen4376" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4377" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9. </hi>And make ye marriages with us, <hi type="italic">and</hi> give your daughters unto us, and take our daughters unto you.<div eID="gen4377" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4378" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9. </hi>Et affinitatem contrahite nobiscum: filias vestras dabitis nobis, et filias nostras accipietis vobis.<div eID="gen4378" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4379" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10. </hi>And ye shall dwell with us: and the land shall be before you; dwell and trade ye therein, and get you possessions therein.<div eID="gen4379" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4380" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10. </hi>Et nobiscum habitabitis, et terra erit coram vibis, habitate, et negotiamini in ea, et possessiones acquirite in ea.<div eID="gen4380" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4381" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11. </hi>And Shechem said unto her father and unto her brethren, Let me find grace in your eyes, and what ye shall say unto me I will give.<div eID="gen4381" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4382" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11. </hi>Adhaec dixit Sechem ad patrem ejus, et ad fratres ejus, Inveniam gratiam in oculis vestris: et quod dixeritis mihi, dabo.<div eID="gen4382" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4383" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12. </hi>Ask me never so much dowry and gift, and I will give according as ye shall say unto me: but give me the damsel to wife.<div eID="gen4383" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4384" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12. </hi>Augete mihi valde dotem, et donum: et dabo quemadmodum dixeritis mihi, et date mihi puellam in uxorem.<div eID="gen4384" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4385" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13. </hi>And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and said, because he had defiled Dinah their sister:<div eID="gen4385" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4386" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13. </hi>Et responderunt filii Iahacob ad Sechem et Hamor patrem ejus in dolo, et loquuti sunt, (quia violaverat Dinah sororem suam,)<div eID="gen4386" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4387" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14. </hi>And they said unto them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that <hi type="italic">were</hi> a reproach unto us:<div eID="gen4387" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4388" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14. </hi>Et dixerunt ad eos, Non possumus facere hoc, ut demus sorerem nostram viro, cui est praeputium: quia opprobrium esset nobis.<div eID="gen4388" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4389" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15. </hi>But in this will we consent unto you: If ye will be as we <hi type="italic">be</hi>, that every male of you be circumcised;<div eID="gen4389" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4390" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15. </hi>Veruntamen in hoc acquiescemus vobis, si fueritis sicut nos, ut circumcidatur in vobis omnis masculus.<div eID="gen4390" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4391" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16. </hi>Then will we give our daughters unto you, and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.<div eID="gen4391" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4392" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16. </hi>Et dabimus filias nostras vobis, et filias vestras capiemus nobis: et habitabimus vobiscum, et erimus in populum unum.<div eID="gen4392" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4393" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17. </hi>But if ye will not hearken unto us, to be circumcised; then will we take our daughter, and we will be gone.<div eID="gen4393" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4394" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17. </hi>Quodsi non obedieritis nobis, ut circumcidamini: capiemus filiam nostram et recedemus.<div eID="gen4394" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4395" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18. </hi>And their words pleased Hamor, and Shechem Hamor’s son.<div eID="gen4395" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4396" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18. </hi>Et placuerunt verba eorum in oculis Hamor, et in oculis Sechem filii Hamor.<div eID="gen4396" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4397" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19. </hi>And the young man deferred not to do the thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter: and he <hi type="italic">was</hi> more honourable than all the house of his father.<div eID="gen4397" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4398" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19. </hi>Nec tardavit juvenis ad perficiendum negotium, quia complacuerat ei in filia Iahacob: et ipse erat honorabilis prae tota domo patris sui.<div eID="gen4398" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4399" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20. </hi>And Hamor and Shechem his son came unto the gate of their city, and communed with the men of their city, saying,<div eID="gen4399" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4400" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20. </hi>Et venit Hamor et Sechem filius ejus ad portam civitatis suae, et loquuti sunt ad viros civitatis suae, dicendo,<div eID="gen4400" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4401" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21. </hi>These men <hi type="italic">are</hi> peaceable with us; therefore let them dwell in the land, and trade therein; for the land, behold, <hi type="italic">it is</hi> large enough for them; let us take their daughters to us for wives, and let us give them our daughters.<div eID="gen4401" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4402" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21. </hi>Viri isti pacati sunt nobiscum, et habitabunt in terra, et negotiabuntur in ea (et terra ecce, lata est spatiis ante eos) filias eorum accipiemus nobis in uxores, et filias nostras dabimus eis.<div eID="gen4402" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4403" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22. </hi>Only herein will the men consent unto us for to dwell with us, to be one people, if every male among us be circumcised, as they <hi type="italic">are</hi> circumcised.<div eID="gen4403" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4404" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22. </hi>Veruntamen in hoc acquiescent nobis viri, ut habitent nobiscum, ut sint populus unus, quando circumcisus erit in nobis omnis masculus, quemadmodum ipsi sunt circumcisi.<div eID="gen4404" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4405" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23. </hi><hi type="italic">Shall</hi> not their cattle and their substance and every beast of theirs <hi type="italic">be</hi> ours? only let us consent unto them, and they will dwell with us.<div eID="gen4405" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4406" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23. </hi>Greges eorum, et substantia eorum et omnia jumenta eorum, nonne nostra erunt? tantum acquiescamus eis, et habitabunt nobiscum.<div eID="gen4406" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4407" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24. </hi>And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city; and every male was circumcised, all that went out of the gate of his city.<div eID="gen4407" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4408" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24. </hi>Et assensi sunt Hamor et Sechem filio ejus, omnes qui egrediebantur per portam civitatis ejus: et circumciderunt se omnis masculus, omnes egredientes per portam civitatis ejus.<div eID="gen4408" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4409" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25. </hi>And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.<div eID="gen4409" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4410" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25. </hi>Et fuit in die tertia, quum essent ipsi dolore affecti, acceperunt duo filii Iahacob Simhon et Levi fratres Dinah, quisque gladium suum, et venerunt ad civitatem confidenter, et occiderunt omnem masculum.<div eID="gen4410" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4411" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26. </hi>And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went out.<div eID="gen4411" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4412" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26. </hi>Et Hamor et Sechem filium ejus occiderunt acie gladii, et tulerunt Dinah e domo Sechem et egressi sunt.<div eID="gen4412" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4413" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">27. </hi>The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and spoiled the city, because they had defiled their sister.<div eID="gen4413" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4414" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">27. </hi>Filii Iahacob progressi sunt super occisos, et praedati sunt urbem, quia violaverant sororem suam.<div eID="gen4414" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4415" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28. </hi>They took their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses, and that which <hi type="italic">was</hi> in the city, and that which                   <ns0:head>CHAP. XXXIII.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1 AND Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 32. 6.</ns0:note> Esau came, and with him four hundred men: and he divided the children unto Leah, and unto Rachel, and unto the two handmaids.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And he put the handmaids, and their children foremost, and Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph hindermost <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Placing his best beloved in the last and safest place.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 And he passed over before them <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Exposing himself to the first and greatest hazard for the security of his Wives and Children.</ns0:note>, and bow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed himself to the ground seven times, untill he came near to his brother.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 And Esau ran to meet him, and imbraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him, and they wept.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And he lift up his eyes, and saw the Women, and the Children, and said, Who are those <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> to the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> with thee! and he said, The Children which God hath graciously given thy servant.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 Then the handmaidens came near, they and their children, and they bowed themselves.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 And Leah also with her children came near, and bowed themselves: and after came Joseph near and Rachel, and they bowed themselves.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And he said, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> What is all this <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>and to thee.</ns0:note> what meanest thou by all this drove, which I met? <ns0:note n="†" place="bottom">He knew his meaning before from the servants mouths, but he asks that he might both be more certainly informed of the Truth, and have an occasion for a civil refusal of the gift.</ns0:note> And he said, <ns0:hi>These are</ns0:hi> to<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> find grace in the sight of my Lord.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 And Esau said, I have enough, my brother: <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> be that to thee that is <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> keep that thou hast unto thy self <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">I neither need it for my use, nor desire it as a compensa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion for thy former injuries.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee: If now I have found grace in thy sight, then receive my present at my hand: for therefore <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>For</ns0:hi> I therefore tender it unto thee, and humbly beg thy acceptance of it, <ns0:hi>because:</ns0:hi> for the Hebrew <ns0:hi>Al-cen</ns0:hi> is used <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 14. 43. and elsewhere.</ns0:note> I have seen thy face, as though I had seen the face of God <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">It is in a manner as pleasant a sight to me as the sight of God himself, because in thy re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />conciled face I see the face and favour of God thus manifested unto me.</ns0:note>: and thou wast pleased with me.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 Take, I pray thee, my blessing <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">This gift which as I received from Gods blessing, so I hearti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly give it to thee with my blessing and prayer that God would abundantly bless it to thee. Gifts are oft called <ns0:hi>blessings,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 15. 19. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 25. 27. and 30. 26.</ns0:note> that is brought to thee; because God hath dealt graci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ously with me, and because I have <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> all things.</ns0:note> enough: and he urged him, and he took it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And he said, Let us take our journey, and let us go, and I will go before thee <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Or rather, <ns0:hi>beside thee,</ns0:hi> so as to keep thee company, or to keep pace with thee.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And he said unto him, My Lord knoweth, that the children are tender <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The eldest of them, <ns0:hi>Reuben,</ns0:hi> not being yet fourteen years old.</ns0:note>, and the flocks and herds with young are with me <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>upon me,</ns0:hi> i. e. committed to my care, to be ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />naged as their necessities require. See <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 40. 11.</ns0:note>: and if men should overdrive them one day, all the flock will die.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 Let my Lord, I pray thee, pass over before his servant, and I will lead on softly, according <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to the foot of the work<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                        </ns0:hi> &c. <ns0:hi>and according to the foot of the children.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> as the cattle that goeth before me, and the children be able to endure, until I come unto my Lord unto Seir <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">We do not read that <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> did according to this promise or insinuation go to <ns0:hi>Seir,</ns0:hi> either therefore he changed his first in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tentions for some weighty reasons or upon warning from God: Or, he used this onely as a pretence, which we should not too easily believe of so good a man, especially after such dangers and deliverances: or rather he did perform this promise, though the Scripture be silent of it, as it is of many other historical passages, and as it is here concerning <ns0:hi>Iacobs</ns0:hi> visiting of his father <ns0:hi>Isaac,</ns0:hi> which is not mentioned till ten years after this time, and yet it is utterly incredible that <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> should be so near to his dear and worthy Father for so long a time together, and not once give him a visit.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And Esau said, Let me now <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> set or place.</ns0:note> leave with thee <ns0:hi>some</ns0:hi> of the folk that are with me: And he said, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore is this?</ns0:note> what needeth it? <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 34. 11.</ns0:note> let me find grace in the sight of my Lord.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 So Esau returned that day, on his way un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to Seir.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And Jacob journyed to Succoth, and built him an house <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Which doubtless was some slight building, because he in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tended not to stay there.</ns0:note>, and made booths for his cattle: therefore the name of the place is called <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>booths.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Succoth.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 And Jacob came to Shalem <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Most take it for the proper name of a place belonging to <ns0:hi>Shechem,</ns0:hi> as it here follows, called <ns0:hi>Salim, Iohn</ns0:hi> 3. 23. and <ns0:hi>Si<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chem</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Sychar, Iohn</ns0:hi> 4. 5. But others take it for an appella<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tive noun, and render the place thus, <ns0:hi>he came safe,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>whole to the City of Shechem:</ns0:hi> to note either that he was then cured of the lameness which the Angel gave him: Or rather, to note the good providence of God that had brought him safe in his Person, Family, and Estate, through all his dangers; first from <ns0:hi>Laban,</ns0:hi> then from <ns0:hi>Esau</ns0:hi> till he came to this place, where it seems he intended to make his abode for a good while, had not the following miscarriages obliged him to remove.</ns0:note>, a City of <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Called Act. 7. 16. <ns0:hi>Sychem.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan-Aram, and pitched his tent before the City <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Near to it, but not in it, for the conveniency of his Cattle.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Josh. 24. 32.</ns0:note> he bought <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">For his present possession and use; for the right which he had to it was onely in Reversion after the time that God had allotted for it.</ns0:note> a parcel of a field where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Subjects, called his <ns0:hi>Children</ns0:hi> to note the duty which they owed to him, and the Care and Affecti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on that he owed to them. Compare <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 11. 12.</ns0:note> of <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">called Acts 7. 16. Emor.</ns0:note> Hamor, Shechems father, for an hun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dred <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> lambs.</ns0:note> pieces of money <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The word is used onely here and <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 24. 32. <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 42. 11. and it may signifie either <ns0:hi>Lambs,</ns0:hi> given in way of exchange for it, or pieces of money, which seems more probable, both by com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />paring <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 7. 16. and because money was come into use in that place and time, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 17. 12, 13. and 23. 16. and 47. 16. which were called <ns0:hi>Lambs</ns0:hi> possibly from the figure of a <ns0:hi>Lamb</ns0:hi> stamped upon it, as the <ns0:hi>Athenian</ns0:hi> money was called an <ns0:hi>Oxe</ns0:hi> for the like reason, and as we call a piece of Gold a <ns0:hi>Iaco<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bus,</ns0:hi> because the picture of that King is upon it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 And he erected there an Altar, and called it <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>God the God of Israel.</ns0:hi>
